Hebron is under full Israeli siege, mayor says
item.description:
Hebron is under full Israeli siege, mayor says

Israeli forces have sealed off all entrances to Hebron in the occupied West Bank and forcibly displaced around 2,200 Palestinians from their homes, Mayor Yousef Jaabari told Middle East Eye on Saturday evening.

“Hebron is now a disaster zone. The occupation has closed all entrances to the city. No one can enter or leave,” Jaabari said, accusing Israel of imposing collective punishment following a deadly shooting on Friday.

Two suspected Palestinians opened fire on Israeli troops at a checkpoint in northern Hebron early in the day near the Farsh al-Hawa checkpoint west of Hebron, killing two soldiers and wounding three others. 

Jaabari said Israeli forces forcibly evicted around 2,200 people, including elderly people, women and children, from Deir Bahala, al-Jalda and surrounding neighbourhoods. The affected area spans approximately 330 dunams and contains more than 490 housing units.

Residents told MEE that soldiers gave families five minutes to leave while videos posted on social media showed Palestinian lorry drivers working together to move goods and supplies out of factories ahead of their demolition by Israeli forces. 

Read more: ‘A disaster zone’: Hebron is under full Israeli siege, mayor says

item.title: Report: Leading officials from Mecca pact to meet Iranian officials in Tehran
item.description:
Report: Leading officials from Mecca pact to meet Iranian officials in Tehran

Top officials from countries involved in the Mecca Pact are expected to meet Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday to discuss regional coordination, Reuters reported citing two sources. 

According to the sources, Saudi Arabia will be represented by Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan by army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir as well as the Turkish head of intelligence.

item.title: Netanyahu warns Iran against 'disrupting' Israeli elections
item.description:
Netanyahu warns Iran against 'disrupting' Israeli elections

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu published a video on Sunday warning "Iran and its proxies" that they would "suffer blows out of all proportion" if they were to target Israel aiming to disrupt the upcoming elections.

"It will be a decisive strike against you," he said, adding that "intelligence" suggested that Iran was planning a disruption.

The statement comes as Israeli head to the first elections since 7 October 2023, which could oust the current cabinet.

item.title: Trump reiterates endorsement of Netanyahu in Israeli elections
item.description:
Trump reiterates endorsement of Netanyahu in Israeli elections

US President Donald Trump on Sunday called on Israelis to cast their ballots for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in upcoming elections, citing the US-Israel war on Iran as an example of "winning together."

"When you go to the Polls please remember that Bibi has been an outstanding Warrior Prime Minister," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

“Vote for Bibi Netanyahu for Prime Minister, we have to finish the job that we started!” he said.

item.title: Why is the Middle East waiting out the Trump presidency?
item.description: There appears to be little prospect of lasting peace between Iran and the United States while Donald Trump remains in the White House. This is a view that an increasing number of serious actors across the region now seem to share. Eight months into Iran war, Washington has neither broken Tehran’s resolve nor found a clear path out. The president’s own remarks point to a narrowing set of options. Trump told TIME he does not believe peace with Iran is ever possible, a striking admission from the leader still expected to negotiate one. item.title: Opposition leader says Netanyahu ‘no longer fit’ to lead Israel
item.description: Just days before pivotal Israeli elections, opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot said Saturday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is “no longer fit” to lead the country, warning that his economic plan to counter potential international sanctions threatens national security, Anadolu reports. On US social media company X, the Yashar party leader accused Netanyahu of turning his attention to “dismantling the Israeli economy for generations ahead” after “dismantling Israeli society and weakening the army.” Eisenkot said Netanyahu’s recent remarks are “conclusive proof that he has lost touch with reality and moved into a world of delusions,” accusing him of proposing preparations to disconnect from the global financial system in response to Israel’s declining international standing. “This is the madness of a man […]

item.title: Israeli army turns Palestinian homes into military posts in West Bank city of Hebron
item.description: Israeli forces turned Palestinian homes into barracks and observation posts after forcing residents to leave the city of Hebron on Saturday, day two of a military operation in the southern occupied West Bank, the official Palestinian news agency Wafa reported, Anadolu reports. Troops took over homes in the Khallat Manna and Dahiyat al-Zaytoun areas of southern Hebron to be used as barracks, official Palestinian news agency Wafa reported, citing sources. They also forced residents from homes in other neighborhoods and used the properties as observation posts, said sources. The evictions follow the forced displacement of hundreds of families since Friday, amid extensive raids, road closures, and tight restrictions on movement.
